sections.content:
Now I can see the structure. The white blocks form a grid pattern at rows {15,21,27,33,39,45} and columns {15,21,27,33,39,45} — a 6×6 lattice with some missing:
Row 15: columns 15,27,33,39 (21 missing)
Row 21: 21,27,33,39,45 (15 missing)
Row 27: 21,27,33,45 (39 missing)
Row 33: 15,21,27,33,39,45 (all)
Row 39: 15,21,27,33,39,45 (all)
Row 45: 15,21,33,39 (27,45 missing)
Gray blocks are at intermediate positions (offset 3), e.g., (15,18),(15,30),(15,36),(18,21),(18,27),(18,39),(21,30),(21,36),(21,42),(24,21),(24,27),(24,33),(24,45),(27,24),(30,33),(30,45),(33,18),(33,24),(33,30),(33,42),(36,15),(36,21),(39,18),(39,24),(39,30),(39,42),(42,21),(42,33),(42,39),(42,45),(45,18),(45,36).
So the maze is a lattice of 3×3 white blocks (nodes) connected by corridors, with gray blocks acting as walls between some of the nodes. The player is currently at (15,21) — this is a lattice node position (white block's former position).
Observed mechanic: pressing RIGHT made the player swap with the white block at (15,21)... wait, the player was at (15,15) and the white block was at (15,21)? No wait — in frame0, was there a white block at (15,21)? Let me check frame0's white list. In frame0, the player was at (15,15) (blue), and the white block was at (15,21)? In the current white list, (15,15) is white (the swapped one). In frame0, (15,15) was blue (player) and (15,21) was white. So the lattice node at (15,21) existed in frame0.
So the mechanic is: the player hops to the nearest white block in the pressed direction, and the white block moves to the player's old position. In effect, the player and the white block swap positions. The gray blocks in between don't block.
But wait — is it "swap with the nearest white block in that direction," or "move to the adjacent lattice node if it's white"? In this case, the distance was 6 (2 lattice steps of 6 apart? No — lattice spacing is 6: 15→21). The player moved exactly 1 lattice step (6 cells) to the right, landing on the white block at (15,21). The gray block at (15,18) is in between, but didn't block.
So effectively: the player moves 1 lattice step (6 cells) in the pressed direction, but only if the target lattice node is a white block (not gray/empty)? And the white block swaps to the player's old position.
Hmm, but why does the white block move? Maybe the mechanic is: the player pushes... no, it's a swap. Or: the white block is a "tile," and the player swaps with it. The player can only move to a position occupied by a white block.
Actually, a simpler interpretation: the player can move to an adjacent lattice node (6 cells in one of the 4 directions) only if that node is a white block. The white block moves to the player's old position (swap). The player's old position becomes a white block (so the player can come back).
Gray blocks = blocked nodes (walls). Empty nodes (no block) = also blocked?
Let me verify with the UP press: the player was at (15,15). The node above would be (9,15) — outside the lattice (the lattice starts at row 15). No white block there → no movement. ✓
The 2nd–5th RIGHT presses: the player is at (15,21). The node to the right is (15,27) — white! But the RIGHT press did nothing?!
Hmm, this contradicts. After the swap, the player is at (15,21) and the white block is at (15,15). The node to the right of the player is (15,27), which is white (still in the list). But the subsequent RIGHTs did nothing.
So the "swap with the nearest white block" theory is also wrong, because (15,27) is white and to the right.
Let me reconsider. Maybe the mechanic is: the player slides in the pressed direction until it hits a white block, and then... no, that's not it.
Alternative: the player moves 1 cell per action, but the frame I'm seeing is... no, the transition showed a jump of +6 columns in a single action.
Wait, let me re-verify the transition: "RIGHT -> ((15, 21), (17, 23))" — after the first RIGHT, the player's top-left is at (15,21). Before: (15,15). So yes, +6.
Hmm, what if the mechanic is: the player swaps with the nearest block (white or gray?) in that direction? In frame0, to the right of the player at (15,15): the nearest block is the gray at (15,18) (distance 3), then the white at (15,21) (distance 6). The player swapped with the white at (15,21), not the gray. So it's not the nearest block.
What if the player moves to the next lattice node, and the lattice node must be white? (15,21) is white → move. Then from (15,21), the next node to the right is (15,27), which is white → should move. But it didn't.
Unless the swap changed something: after the swap, the white block is at (15,15). Maybe the rule is: the player can only move to a white block that is "adjacent through a corridor" — that is, the space between the player and the target must be empty (no gray)? From (15,15) to (15,21): in between is the gray at (15,18) — that's a gray block! So there was a gray in between, yet it still moved.
Hmm, wait, maybe I'm getting the gray/white roles reversed. Let me look at the actual maze image again. In the image, the maze has white blocks and gray blocks. The player is blue.
Let me think about the corridor structure: lattice nodes are at rows/cols {15,21,27,33,39,45}. Between horizontally adjacent nodes (e.g., (15,15) and (15,21)), the intermediate cell (15,18) is either gray (wall) or empty (passage). In frame0, (15,18) was gray. And the player moved from (15,15) to (15,21) — through the gray?? That's strange.
Wait, maybe I have it backwards: gray = passage, white = wall?? In frame0: the player at (15,15) is adjacent to the white at (15,21)?? No wait, in frame0, was (15,21) white? Let me verify frame0's white list. I only printed the current frame's list. Let me get frame0's list.
Actually, from the diff: the only changes in rows 15–17 are the blue↔white swap at columns 15–17 and 21–23. So in frame0, (15,21) was white, and (15,15) was blue. The gray at (15,18) is unchanged.
So the player jumped over the gray block at (15,18) and swapped with the white at (15,21).
New idea: maybe the mechanic is a "slide until you hit a wall," where gray = wall and white = floor, and the player slides until just before a wall... let me test: the player at (15,15) slides right. The sprite is 3 wide. It can move right as long as the 3×3 region is free (not gray, not white?). If white is also a wall, the player should stop at (15,17) (just before the white at (15,21))? But the player ended up exactly at (15,21), where the white was. And the white moved to (15,15).
So it's a swap. The player swaps with the white block. The white block is like a "ghost" tile that the player can swap with.
Then why didn't the 2nd RIGHT swap with the white at (15,27)?
Maybe... the swap only happens if the white block is "adjacent" in the lattice sense, and the intermediate node must be empty (not gray)? From (15,21) to (15,27): the intermediate is (15,24) — is there a gray at (15,24)? Gray list: (15,18),(15,30),(15,36) — no (15,24). So the intermediate is empty. Hmm, so it should be swappable.
I'm confused. Let me look at the actual transition frames more carefully — maybe the 2nd–5th RIGHTs did something else (like moving a white block) that I missed. The full-board diff (frame0 vs current) only showed the swap and the HUD. So the 2nd–5th RIGHTs did nothing to the board.
Hmm, wait. Maybe the batch action wasn't executed as I assumed. The system said "executed actions: UP, UP, UP, RIGHT, RIGHT, RIGHT, RIGHT, RIGHT" — 8 actions. And the transitions show 8 entries: 3 UPs (no movement), 5 RIGHTs (the first one jumped, the rest no movement).
Let me reconsider: maybe the player's movement is 1 cell per action, and the jump is because... the player's sprite is 3×3, and the "player" position is tracked by the eye (c)? The eye was at (16,16) in frame0 and is now at (16,22). Also +6.
OK, another thought: maybe the game has a "momentum/slide" mechanic: pressing RIGHT makes the player slide right until it collides with something (a wall = gray or white?), and then the player... no, the player ended up exactly at the white block's position, and the white block moved.
Actually — wait. What if the white block isn't a separate object, and the "swap" is actually: the player slides right through the gray (gray is passable!), and the white block at (15,21) is... hmm, but then why did the white move to (15,15)?
Let me look at the diff once more: ('b','W'):8 means 8 cells changed from blue to white (the player's old position became white), ('W','b'):8 (the old white position became blue), ('c','W'):1, ('W','c'):1 (the eye). So yes, a complete swap of the 3×3 sprites.
Hypothesis: this is a "push/swap" game where the player swaps with any white block in the pressed direction (the nearest one), regardless of what's in between. Then from (15,21), pressing RIGHT should swap with the white at (15,27). But it didn't.
Unless the swap only works if the white block is the nearest block in that direction, and gray blocks block the line of sight? From (15,21) looking right: the nearest block is the white at (15,27) (no gray in between; the gray at (15,30) is further). So it should swap. But it didn't.
Hmm, let me question the assumption that (15,27) is white in the current frame. Current white list: (15,15),(15,27),(15,33),(15,39). Yes, (15,27) is white.
So why did the 2nd RIGHT do nothing? Maybe the swap has a cooldown? Or the swap only happens if the player's old position is...? Or the white block at (15,15) (the one that just moved) is now "locked"?
Or maybe the mechanic is different: the player moves to the next lattice node in the pressed direction, and that node must be empty (black) — that is, the player moves into an empty node, and the white block... no, the player moved into the white block's position.
Let me try yet another interpretation: the white blocks are the player's "home" tiles, and the game is: the player can move to any white tile in the same row/column (like a rook's move), and the white tile moves to the player's old position (the tiles are like a sliding puzzle). The first RIGHT: the player at (15,15) moves right along row 15 to the next white tile at (15,21). ✓. The 2nd RIGHT: the player at (15,21) moves right to the next white tile at (15,27) — should work but didn't.
I'm stuck on why the 2nd RIGHT failed. Let me experiment: press RIGHT once now and observe. Also press DOWN once and observe. These probes will clarify the mechanic. Actually, let me press RIGHT and check the result.
Actually, wait — maybe the issue is: the batch's actions were executed, but the game only processes one action per "step," and the rest were... no, the transitions show all 8.
Hmm, or maybe the 2nd–5th RIGHTs were blocked because... the player is now "on top of" the white block's former position, and the rule is that the player can only swap with a white block if the white block is adjacent in the lattice (distance 6) AND the player's current position is a "valid node"? The player is at (15,21), which is a valid node. The white at (15,27) is adjacent. It should work.
Let me probe: execute a single RIGHT and see what happens.

sections.label: ASSISTANT
sections.content: The lattice structure is clear: white 3×3 blocks are located at rows/columns {15,21,27,33,39,45}, with gray blocks placed between some of the nodes. The first RIGHT swapped the player with the white block at the next lattice node, but the subsequent RIGHTs did nothing (even though there's a white block at (15,27)). Currently probing with a single RIGHT to identify the rules.

sections.label: TOOL CALL: python
sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
res = action(['RIGHT'])
def bbox(frame, ch='b'):
    lines = frame.ascii.split('\n')
    pts = [(r,c) for r in range(64) for c in range(64) if lines[r][c]==ch]
    return (min(pts), max(pts)) if pts else None
print("after RIGHT:", bbox(current_frame), "changed:", res.get('board_changed'))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
